XSYNC USER MANUALSECTION 1

xs(1) ​

The xsync manual

Parallel file transfers, familiar commands, and progress you can read.

NAME ​

xs — fast, parallel rsync work-alike for macOS and Linux. The xsync project installs a single executable, xs.

SYNOPSIS ​

Command forms
sh
xs [OPTION]... SRC [SRC]... DEST
xs [OPTION]... SRC
xs [OPTION]... SRC [SRC]... [USER@]HOST:DEST
xs [OPTION]... [USER@]HOST:SRC [DEST]

DESCRIPTION ​

xsync copies file trees locally or over SSH. It uses a C++20 engine, parallel workers, a native transfer protocol, and a live progress display on stderr. A single source argument lists entries instead of copying them.

Use the options you already know from rsync. Native transfers require xsync on both machines. Missing remote support and unsupported options can delegate to a real rsync from PATH; --no-fallback requests native-only execution.

EXAMPLES ​

Copy a directory’s contents
sh
xs -aP src/ dst/
Push over SSH
sh
xs -azP src/ user@host:/backup/src/
Pull over SSH
sh
xs -azP user@host:/data/ data/
Preview a mirror before executing
sh
xs -ani --delete src/ dst/

The slash on src/ means copy its contents. -P enables partial retention and progress. -n previews changes without writing.

OPTIONS ​

Archive mode, -a, means -rlptgoD. Add -H, -A, or -X when you need hard links, ACLs, or extended attributes. Use -j N to choose worker threads.

See the complete option reference, generated from the executable’s actual --help.
